title: How to Speak Bosnian: Grammar
summary: A parallel handbook. Not Book 2. English hangs meaning on little words and word order. Bosnian hangs it on the end of the word. Same small word set as Book 1.
pedagogy: One system per chapter. English contrast first. Small tables. No civic notes. No cat plot. No Lesson A and Lesson B.

parts.title: Endings, not word order
parts.focus: Gender, then the cases, then the preposition map.

parts.title: What has to match
parts.focus: Adjectives and pronouns take the same ride as the noun.

parts.title: The verb machine
parts.focus: Present, aspect, past, future, and commands.

parts.title: How a Bosnian sentence actually runs
parts.focus: Clitics in second place, then the English-shaped mistakes.

chapters.title: Zašto je teško?
chapters.theme: A map of four systems. English keeps the word still. Bosnian dresses it again.

chapters.title: Zašto je kahva ona?
chapters.theme: Coffee is she because of the last letter, not because the drink is girly.

chapters.title: Nominativ i akuzativ
chapters.titleEn: Subject and the thing you want
chapters.theme: Želim kahvu shows who does the wanting versus the thing you want.

chapters.title: Genitiv
chapters.theme: Nema kahve shows that English of is a separate word here.

chapters.title: Dativ i lokativ
chapters.theme: Dajem Ani kahvu shows giving to someone, sitting at a place, and in versus into.

chapters.title: Instrumental, vokativ, mapa
chapters.theme: S kahvom and Emire finish with and calling, then one map points the little words at jobs you already own.

chapters.title: Pridjevi
chapters.theme: Moja kahva becomes moju kahvu when matching my rides with pile and job.

chapters.title: Zamjenice
chapters.theme: Mene versus me shows the long form after a little word like kod.

chapters.title: Prezent
chapters.theme: Želim, želiš, and želi show that who hangs on the end of the doing-word.

chapters.title: Vid
chapters.theme: English eat splits into two Bosnian verbs, one open along the way and one sealed when the plate is done.

chapters.title: Prošlost
chapters.theme: Past tense hangs sam with -o, -la, or -lo so Emir and Ana split on the doing-word.

chapters.title: Budućnost i naredbe
chapters.theme: Tomorrow uses ću, commands split blunt and polite, and moći, morati, trebati, and htjeti cover can, must, need, and want.

chapters.title: Enklitike
chapters.theme: Ja se zovem works. Se zovem does not.

chapters.title: Šta Englezi krivo kažu
chapters.theme: This mixed review walks the whole-book map without opening a new system.
